subject: Data Structures
title: Discover Binary Search Trees
description: Discover how a Binary Search Tree places values by comparing them with existing nodes.

mission.title: Build the Search Tree
mission.description: Use comparisons to place each value on the left or right side of the tree.

quiz.question: A BST node contains 50. Where should 30 be placed?

discovery.title: Comparisons Organize the Tree
discovery.summary: A Binary Search Tree organizes values using comparisons. Smaller values go into the left subtree and larger values go into the right subtree.

sections.title: What is a Binary Search Tree?
sections.content: A Binary Search Tree, or BST, stores values in nodes arranged by comparison.

sections.title: Root, parent, and child
sections.content: The first node is the root. A node above another is its parent, and the connected node below is its child.

sections.title: Left and right children
sections.content: Each node can have a left child and a right child.

sections.title: Smaller values go left
sections.content: When inserting a smaller value, move to the left child.

sections.title: Larger values go right
sections.content: When inserting a larger value, move to the right child.

sections.title: Searching and inserting
sections.content: Both searching and inserting follow comparisons from the root until the correct position is reached.

sections.title: Search complexity
sections.content: A balanced BST has average search time O(log n). A badly unbalanced tree can degrade to O(n).

alternate_explanations.title: Think of a choose-your-path sign
alternate_explanations.content: Each tree node is a signpost. A smaller number follows the LEFT path, while a larger number follows the RIGHT path.

alternate_explanations.title: Place values one at a time
alternate_explanations.content: Insert 50 first. Insert 30: it is smaller, so it goes left. Insert 70: it is larger, so it goes right. Insert 40: go left from 50, then right from 30.

introduction.title: Meet the Binary Search Tree
introduction.content: A Binary Search Tree organizes values so comparisons tell you which direction to go. Smaller values go left and larger values go right.
points: The first value becomes the root.
Each comparison chooses LEFT or RIGHT.
You will insert values and see their paths.

worked_example.title: Place one value by comparison
worked_example.content: Insertion does not guess a position. It follows comparisons from the root until an empty child position is found.

steps.explanation: 30 is smaller than the root, so it follows the left path.
The left position was empty, so 30 lands there.

worked_example.conclusion: Every insertion follows the same smaller-left, larger-right rule.

next.title: Insert the sequence below.
next.content: Watch each comparison before the next node appears.

action_explanations.insert-root: The first value becomes the root, where every later comparison begins.
action_explanations.insert-smaller: A smaller value follows the left side of the tree.
action_explanations.insert-larger: A larger value follows the right side of the tree.
action_explanations.follow-comparisons: Comparisons continue until an empty child position gives the value a home.
action_explanations.build-tree: The completed tree keeps smaller values left and larger values right at every node.

challenge.title: BST Challenge
challenge.start_message: Use comparisons to build the requested part of the tree.
challenge.continue_message: Challenge complete. Keep inserting values to explore more paths.

phases.title: Build the first split
phases.instruction: Create a root with one smaller left child and one larger right child.
phases.feedback: Compare each new value with the root before inserting it.

phases.title: Finish the branches
phases.instruction: Continue inserting until each side has its smaller and larger child.
phases.feedback: Follow the highlighted comparison path until an empty child position appears.

recall.title: Recall
recall.prompt: In your own words, why does a BST place a smaller value on the left?
recall.empty_message: Write a short explanation before submitting.
recall.model_answer: Keeping smaller values on the left and larger values on the right preserves an ordered structure, so comparisons can guide searching and insertion.

guidance.start_message: Insert the short sequence and watch each comparison choose a branch.

items.content: Compare every new value with the root before choosing left or right.

phases.title: Build the first split
phases.instruction: Insert 50, 30, then 70 to make a root with two children.
phases.feedback: Follow the highlighted comparison path before each insertion.

guidance.start_message: Predict each value's branch yourself, then insert it.

items.content: Smaller moves left; larger moves right at every node you visit.

phases.title: Place each value
phases.instruction: Build the requested five-node BST without a guided route.
phases.feedback: At each node, compare the incoming value before moving again.

guidance.start_message: Build the target tree from a new insertion sequence with no hints.

phases.title: Build the target BST
phases.instruction: Insert every value and preserve the BST ordering rule.

target.label: TARGET TREE
target.description: Each smaller branch must remain left of its parent; each larger branch right.

phases.feedback: Do not stop at the root: follow comparisons until an empty child position appears.

guidance.start_message: This insertion sequence is randomized. Build the tree independently.

phases.title: Master a new BST
phases.instruction: Use the randomized sequence to construct the final BST.

target.label: TARGET TREE
target.description: Use comparisons—not position guessing—to determine every child.

phases.feedback: Every insertion starts at the root and follows the ordering rule.

thinking.title: Predict the final tree
thinking.instruction: Simulate each insertion before the tree is drawn.
thinking.do_not_execute: Do not insert yet. Decide each parent-child relationship mentally.

prediction_fields.label: Parent → child links
prediction_fields.prompt: List the final links, separated by commas (for example 50→30, 50→70).

thinking.replay_message: Now watch each insertion build the tree.

solve.title: Expert BST
solve.instruction: Build the randomized tree with no hints. Structural correctness is the score.
solve.operation_rule: Each value follows comparisons from the root until an empty child position is found.
solve.feedback: Use the BST rule at every node, not only at the root.
solve.solved_result: The randomized BST structure is complete.
